olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement:
The product of two of the four roots of the quartic equation
$$x^4-18x^3+kx^2+200x-1984=0$$
is $-32$. Determine the value of $k$.

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement:
The geometric mean of any set of $m$ non-negative numbers is the $m$-th root of their product.

(i) For which positive integers $n$ is there a finite set $S_n$ of $n$ distinct positive integers such that the geometric mean of any subset of $S_n$ is an integer?

(ii) Is there an infinite set $S$ of distinct positive integers such that the geometric mean of any finite subset of $S$ is an integer?

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement:
Points $P,A,B,C,$ and $D$ are five distinct points in space such that
$$\angle APB=\angle BPC=\angle CPD=\angle DPA=\theta,$$
where $\theta$ is a given acute angle. Determine the greatest and least possible values of
$$\angle APC+\angle BPD.$$

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: A difficult mathematical competition consisted of a Part I and a Part II with a combined total of $28$ problems. Each contestant solved $7$ problems altogether. For each pair of problems, there were exactly two contestants who solved both of them. Prove that there was a contestant who, in Part I, solved either no problems or at least four problems.

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement:
Let $P(x)$ be a polynomial of degree $3n$ such that
$$P(0)=P(3)=\cdots=P(3n)=2,$$
$$P(1)=P(4)=\cdots=P(3n-2)=1,$$
$$P(2)=P(5)=\cdots=P(3n-1)=0,$$
and
$$P(3n+1)=730.$$
Determine $n$.
